# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22 (Bi-Vb Pc22)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc22
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22
**Title (English, from literature):** Making an oversize bathing robe
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc22

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22, titled *Udakasāṭika* ("Making an oversize bathing robe"), establishes the permissible dimensions for a nun's bathing cloth (*udakasātikā*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. Under this rule, a nun who has a bathing robe constructed must adhere to the standard measure—defined in the rule text as four Buddha spans in length and two and a half in width—and committing to make an oversized garment requires confession of a pācittiya offense [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule constitutes the only *chedanaka-pācittiya* in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga; it uniquely mandates an additional remedial consequence prior to confession, requiring that the oversized robe first be cut down to the permitted measurements, while the *anāpatti* clause exempts robes made smaller than the standard dimensions [Hüsken 1997].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide transmission across early Buddhist monastic codes, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (Pc 22), the Khandhaka (Kd 8, Cīvarakkhandhaka), the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya (Bi-Vb Pc 102), the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (Bi-Vb Pc 128), the Mahāsāṅghika Vinaya (Bi-Vb Pc 75), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (Pc 75) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus confirms cross-language text alignments with Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* materials and the Tibetan *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) [DharmaNexus]. Domestically within the Pali Tipiṭaka, DharmaNexus highlights extensive formulaic text reuse with analogous sizing rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (most prominently Pācittiyas 87, 88, 89, 90, and 91), sections of the Parivāra, and later Vinaya commentaries and subcommentaries such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
